root_cause.text: Use of cancel_work_sync() instead of disable_work_sync() in espintcp_close() leaves the work item enabled, allowing it to be re-scheduled (e.g., via espintcp_write_space()) after cancellation, leading to a use-after-free when the freed context or socket is accessed.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly describes the race: after cancel_work_sync() returns, espintcp_write_space() on another CPU can schedule the work, and the worker may then dereference freed espintcp ctx or sk. The patch replaces cancel_work_sync() with disable_work_sync(), which both cancels and disables future scheduling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Change from cancel_work_sync to disable_work_sync in espintcp_close to prevent work re-queuing after close, fixing a potential use-after-free race.
intent_record.how: Instead of just canceling and waiting for the work to complete but allowing it to be re-queued, the new call disables the work entirely so it cannot be re-queued, thereby ensuring the work item is fully shut down during close.

candidates.rationale: Using cancel_work_sync does not disable the work item, allowing it to be re-scheduled after close, leading to use-after-free when the freed context is accessed.

bic_trace_step.reason: In espintcp_close (line ~489), cancel_work_sync(&ctx->work) is used, which does not prevent the work item from being re-scheduled. The work can be re-scheduled via espintcp_write_space() (line ~392) which calls schedule_work(&ctx->work). Since no flag or mechanism prevents re-scheduling after cancellation, a use-after-free can occur when the work executes after the context is freed.
